description: A fire support line is one of four lines for the coordination of fires. The headquarters of a ground force, of an amphibious force or of the two forces together sets it. On the far side of a coordinated fire line (CFL), in the boundaries of its headquarters, standard indirect fires can occur without more coordination. Other forces should coordinate their fires on the far side of a fire support coordination line (FSCL) with its commander. A restrictive fire line (RFL) between friendly forces that come together prevents fires and their effects across it without coordination. Between a battlefield coordination line (BCL) and the FSCL, Marine aircraft can attack surface targets without approval from the ground combat element (GCE) commander.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this fire support line is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this fire support line has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this fire support line and its local conditions, as free text.

establishing_authority.description: This field identifies the headquarters that set the line.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the line: geographic positions in sequence. A `geojson` geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.

id.description: This field identifies this fire support line. Other records and orders use it to refer to this fire support line.

name.description: This field gives the name of this fire support line, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this fire support line, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this fire support line. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: This field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.

x-enum-descriptions.BCL: A battlefield coordination line (BCL) is a fire support coordination measure of the Marine Corps. Between it and the fire support coordination line (FSCL), Marine air-ground task force (MAGTF) aviation quickly attacks surface targets of opportunity. The approval of the ground combat element (GCE) commander of the area where the targets are is not necessary. The MAGTF commander establishes the BCL. An airspace coordination area (ACA) or a kill box usually includes the area between the BCL and the FSCL.
x-enum-descriptions.CFL: A coordinated fire line (CFL) is a line that a land headquarters sets. Beyond this line, conventional indirect surface fire support means may fire at any time without further coordination. This is applicable only in the boundaries of the establishing headquarters.
x-enum-descriptions.FSCL: A fire support coordination line (FSCL) is a line in the area of operations (AO) for the coordination of fires by other force elements. A land or amphibious force commander establishes it. These fires can have an effect on the current and planned operations of that commander. Other force elements should coordinate these fires with that commander. The establishing commander should coordinate the line with the affected commanders.
x-enum-descriptions.RFL: A restrictive fire line (RFL) is a line between converging friendly forces, of which one or both may move. It prohibits joint fires and the effects of joint fires across the line without coordination with the affected force. Its function is to prevent friendly fire and the duplication of engagements by the converging forces. The commander common to the converging forces establishes it.

title: Fire support line
